description: Simulated 'today' at tick 0 (day 0, 00:00). The data dictionary states today = 2026-10-05.
Seed of the deterministic random numbers (noise, hourly spreading, delivery hours).
Real milliseconds per simulated hour while running (default 5 s).
Smallest allowed interval between ticks.
Speed presets shown in the top bar.
Pause the simulation when a critical event appears.
Upper limit for 'run N hours' / 'jump' actions.
Display offset of the warehouse (Oman, UTC+4, no DST). The clock itself is an integer tick.
Daily demand noise around the baseline (+/-).
History window (days before the last data day) used as the baseline usage.
Relative demand per hour of day 0-23 (heavier in working hours, light at night). Normalised automatically.
Seasonal items and their peak multiplier: ramps up from ramp_start over ramp_days, holds until season_end, then eases off over decay_days.
One-off demand events (spike factor, days held at full factor, days to ease off).
Baseline window for items with a demand event (the weeks before the spike).
Weeks compared in the anomaly test.
Reference weeks before the recent weeks.
Anomaly when recent weekly usage exceeds this multiple of the prior average.
Ignore anomalies on very small volumes.
Forecast horizon.
How far the stock-out projection looks.
Critical when cover is below this and no PO arrives soon.
A PO arriving within this many days softens 'Critical' to 'Low'.
Low when cover is below this (or stock below safety stock).
Overstock status / alert above this cover.
Expiry alert / status window.
Expiry alert becomes High inside this window.
Expiry alert becomes Critical inside this many hours (when stock would be written off).
Stock-out alert when projected within lead time + this many days.
Stock-out within this many days counts as imminent.
Item category treated as safety items.
Temporary substitute item per item, used in supplier messages.
Review cycle added to the lead time in the reorder point.
Never reorder above this cover.
Order quantity covers lead time + this many days.
For perishables the cover is limited to this share of the shelf life.
Round order quantities up to a multiple per unit.
Categories ranked first inside a criticality class (after stock-out risk).
A rejected PO draft is not proposed again before this many hours...
...unless cover has fallen below this share of the cover at rejection (materially worse).
Emergency POs use this share of the normal lead time (minimum 1 day).
Price premium on emergency purchase orders.
A recommendation left pending this long raises an 'overdue' alert.
Overdue becomes Critical when the stock-out is closer than this.
'Postpone' hides a recommendation for this many hours (it keeps ageing but no overdue alert is raised meanwhile).
How long the Undo button stays on the confirmation toast after a decision.
Zone that receives goods which do not fit in their home zone.
Storage type of requests that can be served from rentable zones.
Below this share of the request no partial offer is made.
Deliveries arrive from this hour...
...until this hour (exclusive). Each PO gets a deterministic hour inside the window.
Remainder of a partially received PO is retried after this many hours.
Lots are usable until the end of this hour on their expiry date; the rest is written off right after.
Hours at which the alert agent runs (cheap rules).
Hours at which the forecast agent runs.
Hours at which the replenishment agent runs.
Hours at which the space optimisation agent runs (also after stock-heavy events).
Older agent_runs rows are pruned.
How many times an agent is run again when its own VERIFY check fails (then a visible warning is raised).
Hours of the day after which the coordinator writes the daily summary card (also after Run analysis and at the start).
How many top risks the daily summary lists.
How many of the latest agent runs show their READ / REASON / ACT / VERIFY steps in the Agent panel.
How many of the latest drafts (supplier orders, replies to companies) the Drafts tab loads.
Older daily summaries are pruned.
Rows per page in the live feed and logs ('load more').
How many days ahead the Space Forecast looks (at least 90).
Safety margin: this share of the space the company does not need stays off the market.
A listing is flagged as squeezed by our own orders only when it is short by more than this share of its area (forecast noise is not a conflict).
Smallest block of space worth listing.
Shortest period worth listing or renting.
Listed areas are rounded down to this step.
How many stacked windows (different areas) are searched per zone.
Space that only becomes free in the future is offered a few days later than the forecast says (forecast error).
Forecast confidence is High when the window ends within this many days.
Forecast confidence is Medium up to this many days; later is Low.
Default time before a space kept vacant is looked at again.
A vacant space is offered for decision again early when the free area grows by this much.
Suggested rent in OMR per m² per month (synthetic assumption: the data has no prices).
Suggested length of a listing in months when the free window has no known end.
Market rent in OMR per m² per month used to simulate demand (synthetic assumption).
Rent up to this much above the market price does not reduce offers.
How fast offers disappear when the rent is above the band, and how fast they come when it is below the market.
Chance that another matching company (beyond the guaranteed minimum) sends an offer at a market price.
Earliest an offer arrives after a listing is published.
Latest an offer arrives after a listing is published.
Chance that a company adapts its area and dates to the listing.
Companies bid within this much around the market price (never above the listing price).
An offer that is not answered expires after this many hours.
Fastest answer of a company to a counter-offer.
Slowest answer of a company to a counter-offer.
Chance that a company accepts a fair counter-offer.
When no space is listed, the public website shows three sample listings, clearly labelled as samples.
Areas (m2) of the sample listings on the public website.
Days in a rental month for income per day.
Hours of the day when the Space Forecast agent runs (every hour by default; it also runs after every decision).
Priority 1: a signed rental comes before a new purchase (leased area is unavailable to purchasing). Off: purchasing ignores rentals.
Priority 3: purchase suggestions nobody approved yet only warn (off). On: they also block listing the space they would need.
Length of a budget period (4 weeks, like the first period in the data). A new period starts automatically when one ends.
Budget of every renewed period. 0 = the same amount as the first period of the data.
Share of the unspent money that moves into the next period (0 = none, 100 = all).
Orders placed earlier and not received yet keep counting against the next period (cash-flow view).
Most emergency spend the manager can approve per period, as a share of the period budget.
A critical (class A) item is an emergency when it runs out within its delivery time plus this many days.
A 'budget is low' alert is raised when the free budget falls below this share of the period budget.
Number of extra SIMULATED companies added to the tenant pool next to the CSV requests (made-up names, areas and prices).
Smallest area a simulated company asks for.
Largest area a simulated company asks for.
Shortest rental a simulated company wants, in months.
Longest rental a simulated company wants, in months.
Earliest start of a simulated company's need, in days after the simulation starts.
Latest start of a simulated company's need, in days after the simulation starts.
Lowest price a simulated company is willing to pay, as a share of the market price (price sensitivity).
Highest price a simulated company is willing to pay, as a share of the market price (price sensitivity).
Share of the simulated companies that ask for storage that is never rented out (cold, hazardous): they are shown as demand we cannot serve.
First part of the made-up names of simulated companies.
Second part of the made-up names of simulated companies.
A published listing at a reasonable price gets at least this many offers within the window.
The window (simulated days after publishing) in which the minimum number of offers arrives.
A company only makes an offer when what it is willing to pay is at least this share of the asking price.
